source_text:
18 Πάντα ποίει διὰ τὸν κύριον, καὶ μὴ ζήτει παρὰ ἀνθρώπων δόξαν, ὅτι δόξα
ἀνθρώπων ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου, δόξα δὲ κυρίου μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
19 Παρθένον πραεῖαν ἀγαπᾷ ὁ κύριος, παρθένος δὲ ὀργίλος μισηθήσεται.
20 Ὑπακούουσα παρθένος ἐλεηθήσεται, ἡ δὲ ἀντιλέγουσα ἰσχυρῶς ἄφρων.
21 Γόγγυσον παρθένον ἀπολεῖ κύριος, τὴν δὲ εὐχάριστον ῥύσεται ἐκ θανάτου.
22 Αἰσχρὸν γέλως καὶ ἐπονείδιστον ἀναισχυντία, πᾶσα δὲ ἄφρων τοῖς
τοιούτοις συμπλέκεται.
23 Ἡ καλλωπίζουσα ἱμάτια αὐτῆς καὶ σωφροσύνης ἐκτὸς ἔσται.
24 Μὴ συναυλίζου κοσμικαῖς, ἵνα μὴ διαστρέψωσι σὴν καρδίαν καὶ ἀκύρους
ποιήσωσι βουλὰς δικαίας.
25 ∆άκρυσιν ἐν νυκτὶ παρακάλει τὸν κύριον, καὶ μηδεὶς αἴσθηται
προσευχομένης σου καὶ εὑρήσεις χάριν.
1
26 Ἐπιθυμία περιπάτων καὶ πόθος οἰκιῶν ἀλλοτρίων ἀνατρέπει κατάστασιν
ψυχῆς καὶ διαφθείρει προθυμίαν αὐτῆς.
27 Πιστὴ παρθένος οὐ δειλιάσει, ἡ δὲ ἄπιστος φεύξεται καὶ τὴν σκιὰν αὐτῆς.
28 Φθόνος τήκει ψυχήν, καὶ ζῆλος κατεσθίει αὐτήν.
29 Καταφρονοῦσα τῆς ἀδελφῆς τῆς ἀσθενούσης καὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ μακρὰν
ἔσται.
30 Μὴ εἴπῃς· ἐμὸν τοῦτο καὶ σὸν τοῦτο. ἐν γὰρ Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τὰ πάντα κοινά.
31 Οὐ περιεργάσῃ ζωὴν ἀλλοτρίαν, καὶ πτώματι ἀδελφῆς σου οὐκ ἐπιχαρήσῃ.
32 Ἐπάρκει δεομέναις παρθένοις, καὶ ἐπὶ εὐγενείᾳ σου μὴ ἐπαίρου.
33 Μὴ προενέγκῃς λόγον ἐκ στόματός σου ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ κυρίου, καὶ μὴ
μετεωρίσῃς τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς σου. ὁ γὰρ κύριος γινώσκει σὴν καρδίαν, καὶ πάντας
τοὺς διαλογισμούς σου σκοπεύει.
thought_title: The Lord's care for the meek and obedient virgin
orientation: Evagrius continues his series of counsels to the consecrated virgin, warning her against anger, luxury, gossip, and worldly distractions, and urging her to seek only the Lord's approval.
pass_a_gloss: All [things] do because of the Lord, and do not seek from men glory, because [the] glory of men [is] as [a] flower of grass, but [the] glory of [the] Lord remains unto the age. [A] meek virgin loves the Lord, but [a] wrathful virgin will be hated. [An] obedient virgin will be shown mercy, but the [one] speaking against [is] exceedingly foolish. [A] grumbling virgin will destroy [the] Lord, but the thankful [one] he will rescue from death. Shameful [is] laughter and disgraceful [is] shamelessness, and every foolish [woman] with such [things] is entangled. The [one] adorning her garments also outside of modesty will be. Do not lodge with worldly [women], so that they may not pervert your heart and make void righteous counsels. With tears in [the] night entreat the Lord, and let no one perceive you praying, and you will find grace. Desire of wanderings and longing for houses of others overturns [the] state of [the] soul and corrupts her eagerness. [A] faithful virgin will not be cowardly, but the faithless [one] will flee even her shadow. Envy melts [the] soul, and jealousy devours her. [The one] despising the sister who is weak also from Christ far will be. Do not say: mine [is] this and yours [is] this. For in Christ Jesus all [things are] common. You will not meddle in [the] life of another, and over [the] fall of your sister you will not rejoice. Give aid to needy virgins, and over your noble birth do not exalt [yourself]. Do not bring forth [a] word from your mouth in [the] assembly of [the] Lord, and do not let your eyes wander. For the Lord knows your heart, and all your thoughts he watches.

choices.english: human praise is like a flower of the grass
choices.why: Keeps the simile's concrete image of grass and flower, matching the source's vivid comparison
rejected: the glory of men is as the flower of the field
human glory is like a fading flower

choices.why: Passive future is kept to show the wrathful virgin receives hatred, not that she hates
Passive of ἐλεέω rendered to show mercy comes to her from outside, not her own act
The Lord is the subject; 'destroy' keeps the strong force of ἀπόλλυμι
The middle voice suggests entanglement as a snare; 'gets tangled up in' captures the reflexive involvement
The future of εἰμί with ἐκτός is rendered with 'end up' to show the resulting state
Aorist middle subjunctive of αἰσθάνομαι; 'notice' keeps the sense of perception without deliberate watching
The verb means to upset or overturn; 'overturns' keeps the physical force applied to the soul's settled state
The verb means to be cowardly or timid; 'will be afraid' is the natural English for the future
The verb means to melt or dissolve; 'melts' keeps the physical image of the soul being consumed
The compound verb means to devour; 'eats up' keeps the consuming force
The verb means to busy oneself about; 'meddle in' captures the intrusive sense

bible_refs.note: δόξα ἀνθρώπων ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου, δόξα δὲ κυρίου μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα echoes the contrast between fading human glory and the enduring word of God
The imagery of the lamp, oil, and bridegroom throughout the work draws on the parable of the ten virgins

pass_b_english: Do everything for the Lord, and do not seek praise from people, because human praise is like a flower of the grass, but the praise of the Lord endures forever. The Lord loves a gentle virgin, but a quick-tempered virgin will be hated. A virgin who obeys will receive mercy, but one who talks back is utterly foolish. The Lord will destroy a grumbling virgin, but he will rescue a thankful one from death. Shameful laughter and shamelessness are disgraceful, and every fool gets tangled up in such things. A woman who adorns her clothes will end up outside modesty as well. Do not live with worldly women, so that they do not twist your heart and make your righteous plans worthless. Plead with the Lord in tears at night, and let no one notice that you are praying, and you will find grace. The desire for wanderings and the longing for other people's houses overturns the settled state of the soul and corrupts its eagerness. A faithful virgin will not be afraid, but an unfaithful one will flee even from her own shadow. Envy melts the soul, and jealousy eats it up. A woman who despises her weak sister will be far from Christ as well. Do not say, "This is mine and that is yours," for in Christ Jesus all things are shared. Do not meddle in another person's life, and do not gloat over your sister's fall. Give aid to virgins in need, and do not boast about your noble birth. Do not speak up with a word from your mouth in the assembly of the Lord, and do not let your eyes roam. For the Lord knows your heart, and he watches all your thoughts.

last_rejected.quote: A woman who adorns her clothes will end up outside modesty as well.
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἡ καλλωπίζουσα ἱμάτια αὐτῆς καὶ σωφροσύνης ἐκτὸς ἔσται.
last_rejected.why: Source says 'adorns her clothes' generally; 'woman' adds a noun not present, and 'as well' is unsupported.
last_rejected.fix: One who adorns her clothes will be outside modesty.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Woman' is implied by feminine participle καλλωπίζουσα; 'as well' (καί) is in source.

last_rejected.quote: A woman who despises her weak sister will be far from Christ as well.
last_rejected.source_quote: Καταφρονοῦσα τῆς ἀδελφῆς τῆς ἀσθενούσης καὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ μακρὰν ἔσται.
last_rejected.why: 'Woman' adds a noun absent in source; 'as well' is unsupported addition.
last_rejected.fix: One who despises her weak sister will be far from Christ.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Woman' implied by feminine participle καταφρονοῦσα; 'as well' reflects καί linking both objects of contempt.

last_rejected.quote: Plead with the Lord in tears at night
last_rejected.source_quote: Δάκρυσιν ἐν νυκτὶ παρακάλει τὸν κύριον
last_rejected.why: παρακάλει is imperative 'call upon/invoke/appeal to', not 'plead with'; 'plead' overstates the urgency and legal connotation. 'Call upon the Lord with tears at night' is more accurate.
last_rejected.fix: Call upon the Lord with tears at night
last_rejected.ruling: παρακάλει covers 'plead/entreat'; 'plead with' is within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: overturns the settled state of the soul
last_rejected.why: κατάστασιν means 'constitution/condition/state' of the soul, not 'settled state'; 'overturns the soul's constitution' or 'upsets the soul's state'. 'Settled state' adds an implication of stability not in the Greek.
last_rejected.fix: overturns the soul's constitution and corrupts its eagerness
last_rejected.ruling: κατάστασιν = 'state/condition'; 'settled state' is reasonable, not a meaning change or loss.

last_rejected.why: προθυμία means 'readiness/zeal/goodwill/forwardness', not 'eagerness' in the positive sense; 'corrupts its zeal' or 'readiness' is better. 'Eagerness' is too neutral/positive.
last_rejected.ruling: προθυμίαν = 'eagerness/zeal'; 'eagerness' is within normal range, not a mistranslation.

last_rejected.quote: and do not let your eyes roam
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ μὴ μετεωρίσῃς τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς σου
last_rejected.why: μετεωρίσῃς means 'lift up/raise' (literally or metaphorically of being haughty or looking around proudly); 'let your eyes roam' captures wandering but loses the 'lifted up/haughty' connotation. 'Do not lift up your eyes' or 'do not look around haughtily' is more accurate.
last_rejected.fix: and do not lift up your eyes
last_rejected.ruling: μετεωρίσῃς can mean 'raise/lift up'; 'let eyes roam' captures wandering sense acceptably.

last_rejected.quote: Shameful laughter and shamelessness are disgraceful
last_rejected.why: Αἰσχρὸν is a neuter predicate ('laughter is shameful'), not an adjective modifying laughter; the English narrows the condemnation to only 'shameful laughter.'
last_rejected.fix: Laughter is shameful and shamelessness is disgraceful
last_rejected.ruling: Αἰσχρὸν γέλως predicates shame on laughter; English 'shameful laughter' conveys the same censure, not a narrower sense.
